name: Daniel Gibney

education.school: Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales (ICAEW)
education.notes: ACA qualification reported as 2001-2004 (secondary source). Professional qualification rather than a university degree; he took the standard route of training in audit/finance before moving into corporate finance.

careerSteps.role: Corporate finance / debt advisory roles (early career)
careerSteps.company: ACA training firm + corporate finance teams
keyDecisions: Trained as an ACA chartered accountant before specialising in corporate finance and debt advisory — the standard high-credibility UK path into investment banking restructuring
lessons: An ACA gives you working-capital and balance-sheet literacy that pure-finance-grad bankers often lack
Debt and restructuring exposes you to fragmented, capital-starved industries that mainstream finance avoids
careerSteps.notes: 15+ years cumulative in corporate finance and debt advisory before founding Ferovinum. Specific employer details not surfaced from public sources beyond the Moelis role.

keyDecisions: Built a senior career in corporate-finance restructuring at a top US boutique investment bank
Restructuring work brought him into direct contact with wine importers, where he observed their capital management challenges — the seed of Ferovinum
Walked away from a well-paid Executive Director restructuring role to start a company in a fragmented, under-financed sector
lessons: Restructuring trains you to value assets that mainstream finance ignores — a useful lens for fragmented physical-goods industries
Structured finance expertise is highly portable into sectors no fintech founder is competing for
The right time to leave a high-comp seat is when you have proprietary insight (wine importers' capital pain) that nobody else does
careerSteps.notes: Executive Director-level role at Moelis London. Comp range is a low-confidence estimate for London restructuring at that level.

keyDecisions: Co-founded Ferovinum with Mitchel Fowler in 2018 — they met over poker games, where Fowler says: 'You get to know somebody pretty well over a poker table.' Gibney adds that poker's emphasis on 'skill, risk and judgement' was a good read on character.

Paired his debt-restructuring lens with Fowler's commodity-trading/structured-finance background (energy, metals, agriculture) — both independently saw the opportunity to 'get money into the wine industry'
Stayed in stealth and self-funded for the first ~2 years rather than raising early
Raised £17.5m Series A in 2022, then secured a $550m asset-backed securitisation programme — the world's first ABS of wine and spirits
Rebranded to Fero in 2025 to broaden beyond wine
lessons: Bootstrapping in stealth is viable when the product is structured finance — you don't need to be loud to validate it
Bringing commodity-style structured finance into a fragmented industry (drinks) is a defensible category-creation move
Domain-adjacent expertise beats domain-native expertise when the gap is financial sophistication, not industry knowledge
Co-founder fit can be sourced outside the office — poker, sport, side communities often surface better signal than LinkedIn
careerSteps.notes: Ferovinum/Fero finances and warehouses wine & spirits inventory for drinks businesses, using structured-finance plumbing rather than pure software. Linklaters-advised $550m ABS programme is positioned as a category first. Now serves 600+ producers, distributors, retailers across 30+ markets.

outcomes.currentStatus: Co-founder & CFO of Fero (formerly Ferovinum). Operates a $550m asset-backed securitisation programme funded by private credit and commercial banks; 600+ clients across 30+ markets.

lessons.lesson: Domain-adjacent expertise (structured finance) transplanted into a fragmented industry (wine & spirits) creates a defensible category.
Stealth + self-funded for ~2 years can be the right path when the product is financial infrastructure, not consumer software.
Leaving a high-comp restructuring role late-career has higher opportunity cost but much higher credibility with lenders.
Co-founder selection from outside professional networks (poker games) produced better signal than recruiting from within Moelis would have.

sources.title: The Buyer — How Ferovinum has tech & funding to transform the drinks industry

notes: Modern fintech-era founder. Unusual UK example of a non-software, structured-finance-first venture — closer to commodities trading and asset-backed lending than to typical SaaS. European context: London restructuring background + ABS expertise is hard for US founders to replicate, giving an EU-native moat in drinks finance. Birth year and university degree (if any, pre-ACA) not surfaced from public sources. No exit yet; net worth is largely paper.
